claims.claim: Negligence is commonly described as failure to use the care a reasonable person would use under the same circumstances, and it can concern acts or omissions when a duty to act exists.
Introductory negligence analysis commonly addresses duty, breach, causation, and harm or damages; some sources distinguish factual cause from proximate cause.
Whether a duty exists and the scope of reasonable care are context- and jurisdiction-dependent; risk-creating conduct, undertakings, and special relationships can be relevant in some settings.
Factual cause is often examined with a but-for inquiry, while proximate cause is a legal limitation often associated with directness or foreseeability.
Damages in civil cases concern a remedy for legally recognized harm or loss; the available remedy and proof vary by claim and jurisdiction.
A general educational overview cannot determine whether a particular accident, business practice, or injury gives rise to liability.
